report:
### Conclusion
Current scientific evidence supports your skepticism: following a vegetarian diet does **not** consistently increase overall life expectancy or reduce all-cause mortality compared with eating meat, particularly when compared against health-conscious meat-eaters.

### Key Findings
1. **No Reduction in All-Cause Mortality:** Systematic reviews and meta-analyses show that while vegetarian diets lower the risk of dying from ischemic heart disease, they exert no statistically significant effect on overall all-cause mortality ([PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34611632/)).
2. **Healthy-User Bias:** Early studies showing longevity advantages in vegetarians (such as Seventh-day Adventist cohorts) were confounded by lifestyle factors. Vegetarians tend to smoke less, consume less alcohol, and exercise more. When studies control for these habits by comparing vegetarians to equally health-conscious meat eaters—such as in the UK EPIC-Oxford study—there is no significant difference in all-cause mortality ([ScienceDirect](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0002916523238332)).
3. **Health Trade-offs:** While vegetarians experience lower rates of heart disease, studies indicate trade-offs in other health outcomes. For instance, long-term prospective cohorts observed that vegetarians had lower risks of heart disease but higher risks of stroke and bone fractures ([BMJ](https://www.bmj.com/content/366/bmj.l4897); [AJCN](https://ajcn.nutrition.org/article/S0002-9165(24)00652-X/fulltext)).

Overall lifestyle—including diet quality, physical activity, and avoiding tobacco—matters far more for overall longevity than simply eliminating meat.

### Sources
- Meta-analysis on vegetarian diet and mortality: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34611632/
- EPIC-Oxford British vegetarian study: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0002916523238332
- BMJ study on heart disease and stroke risk: https://www.bmj.com/content/366/bmj.l4897
- American Journal of Clinical Nutrition cause-specific mortality: https://ajcn.nutrition.org/article/S0002-9165(24)00652-X/fulltext
